text:
According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, Inter and Como are among the Serie A clubs backing Adriano Galliani for FIGC President, while Napoli and Roma continue to support Giovanni Malagò.
Serie A clubs seem split over which FIGC Presidential candidate to back in the election on December 14.
According to Gazzetta, Inter, Atalanta, Como and Sassuolo back ex-Milan and Monza director Galliani, while Napoli, Roma and Bologna support Malagò. All the others are waiting for the upcoming round of talks before making a final decision by November 4.
Serie A candidate for FIGC President: Galliani or Malagò?
According to the report, representatives of 14 Serie A clubs will meet informally today with Inter, Milan, Juventus, Roma, Napoli and Lazio, the only ones not joining.
In June, the vast majority of Serie A clubs backed Malagò, with Lazio the only side not to. However, the situation has quickly changed.
The report claims some clubs are unhappy with Malagò’s decision-making process for key appointments. Given the strong support he had received from Serie A clubs, some thought Malagò would share and discuss his decisions with them, but he didn’t.
From re-hiring Roberto Mancini as head coach to appointing Diana Bianchedi as Delegation Chief, some clubs are unhappy about being left out of the decision-making process, so they are looking for an alternative candidate.
Any candidate with 11 votes from Serie A clubs will become their representative for the FIGC Presidential election on December 14.
The deadline to apply is November 4, so talks and negotiations involving all Serie A clubs are expected to continue in the coming days.
In his latest interview with Repubblica, Malagò didn’t seem concerned about some Serie A clubs withdrawing their support: “I’m calling all the Serie A presidents one by one. I’ve already spoken to 13, and they all guarantee me their support,” he said.
Serie A clubs are among the FIGC components taking part in the election, accounting for 18% of the votes.
The other components are Serie B (6%), Lega Pro (12%), Lega Nazionale Dilettanti (34%), players (20%) and coaches (10%).
A new election was required after it emerged that Malagò was not formally a FIGC member when he was elected on June 22, so he was temporarily appointed FIGC Special Commissioner and called new elections on December 14.
digest_he:
קבוצות הליגה הבכירה באיטליה, הסדרה א, מצויות בחילוקי דעות לקראת הבחירות לתפקיד נשיא התאחדות הכדורגל האיטלקית שייערכו ב-14 בדצמבר. על פי דיווחים בתקשורת, קבוצות כמו אינטר, אטאלנטה וקומו תומכות במועמדותו של אדריאנו גליאני, בעוד שפולה, רומא ובולוניה ממשיכות לתמוך בג'ובאני מאלאגו.

הפיצול בין הקבוצות נוצר בין היתר בשל חוסר שביעות רצון מצד כמה ממועדוני הליגה בנוגע לתהליכי קבלת ההחלטות והמינויים של מאלאגו. המועמדים השונים מקיימים פגישות ודיונים אינטנסיביים במטרה להבטיח את תמיכת המועדונים הנדרשת לקראת המועד האחרון להגשת המועמדות.
